propositions: Three independent code paths (normal fold, rebuild, crash recovery) re-derive identical decisions for candidate listing, snapshot detection, envelope building, retired-file restoration, and git commit, creating maintenance burden and divergence risk.

The snapshot envelope structure and source_event_uuids/compacted_at keys appear duplicated across compact_txn and compact_rebuild, and the snapshot-detection rule (_is_snapshot_path) is inlined and spelled three different ways with bug aea0 exclusion inconsistently applied.

The retired-file rename-back rule and its data-loss guard (from bug e72e) are reimplemented three times across compact_txn, compact_recovery, and rollback paths, each with os.rename and post-check logic.

Consolidating to a single compact_plan module with shared Candidate, envelope, retire, and commit functions eliminates duplication while preserving module-specific crash semantics (rebuild keeps .snapshot-rebuild.bak sentinel; fold keeps abort-and-rollback journal).

A stray non-.json file in a ticket directory is incorrectly processed by rebuild's _partition_rebuild_sources (lacks .json suffix check) and may be cited in source_event_uuids or retired; convergence requires enforcing .json suffix in list_candidates.
All SNAPSHOT-envelope key writes and retired-file renames outside compact_plan must be guarded by explicit # compact-plan-ok: markers to prevent future re-duplication.
